_comment: ENTRY shape: what counts as a pullback. Sweeps the RSI length and the lower band whose DOWNWARD cross opens the trade (20 evaluations). A shorter period dips under the band more often, so signals get more numerous and noisier; a lower band demands a deeper spike, so signals get rarer and more extreme. This is the signal generator itself — run it even when the screen says the filters are dead. Everything else inherits DefaultParams. Run: go run ./cmd/backtest -ticker GAZP -strategy rsi_pullback -interval Minutes30 -calibrate data/params/rsi_pullback/cal_entry.json -out ./reports/GAZP_entry -months 24 -min-trades 20 -test-months 6 -metric profit_factor. GAZP is only the example instrument here: this file sweeps one theme and is ticker-agnostic, so replace -ticker and -out to calibrate another name (e.g. -ticker T -out ./reports/T_entry, adding -refresh on a ticker whose candle cache is short).
